sources.notes: Single column, so the section headings work as anchors directly and no occurrence key is needed — this posted copy carries no table of contents repeating them. The slice runs from §1-1926 to the start of §1-1929, which is the span the page reads. The running heads, the page numbers and the document's own 'Unofficial Version – copied from OSCN.NET version' foot fall inside it and are left as printed: this is the state's own posted copy and it labels itself unofficial, which the page records as a finding rather than repairing.

sources.title: OAC 310:675-7-4, Resident transfers or discharge (excerpt from the state's posted copy of OAC 310 chapter 675)
sources.source_date: document foot: Unofficial – copied from/linked to OAR.STATE.OK.US, September 13, 2020
sources.notes: Anchors are the rule heading and the heading of the rule that follows; the chapter's contents list sets its entries as 'Section 310:675-7-4', so the bare heading form matches the body and nothing else, and no occurrence key is needed. The rule's own bracketed [Source: Amended at ...] history line falls inside the slice. The document also carries a bracketed editor's remark inserted by whoever assembled it, which is reproduced as served. Note for anyone reading the retained history: packets of this state captured before 2026-09-04 title this source OAC 310:675-7-5.1, which is a different rule in the same chapter (Reports to state and federal agencies). The rule this source has always held is 310:675-7-4. The mislabel was ours and the page inherited it; both were corrected 2026-09-04 and the correction is on the page's change log.

sources.title: Oklahoma Department of Human Services, Nursing Home Transfers & Discharges (consumer leaflet, PDF)
sources.notes: Captured whole rather than cut to the two content pages the standing packet holds. The leaflet is a folded brochure, so the extractor's line order follows the panels rather than the reading order, and a page cut would be a judgment about which panels matter — the whole document is a superset, which can only add evidence and never narrows what verifies.

sources.title: OAC 317:30-5-126, Therapeutic leave and hospital leave (Oklahoma Health Care Authority's posted copy of its own rule)
sources.source_date: page states [Revised 09-01-15]; the page's own disclaimer calls this copy unofficial and names the Secretary of State's Office of Administrative Rules as the official publisher of Title 317
sources.notes: Added 2026-09-18, deepening the page, to answer section 02's bed-hold row with the Medicaid payment agency's own rule rather than the Department of Health's readmission provision alone. The rule text on this OHCA policy page sits inside one component, id='text-522564591e' on this build; the scope selector targets that element directly rather than 'body', because 'body' on this page's template pulls in the full site navigation, program menus and footer, none of which bears on the rule. The same text also appears, HTML-escaped, inside a client-side analytics data-layer attribute earlier in the document; that occurrence is not what this scope selector reads and is not the evidence — the rendered element is. If a future recapture reports the selector as absent, the component id has likely changed on a template update, which is capture drift to be re-established (find the new id for the rule heading's containing element), not evidence that the rule moved.
